papers.title: Understanding the implementation and scale up of human papillomavirus testing using self-sampling techniques and point-of-care diagnostics for the screening of cervical cancer in Malawi
papers.abstract: Background: Although cervical cancer is one of the most preventable malignancies worldwide, Malawi remains among the top five countries globally with the highest incidence and mortality rates from cervical cancer. The country’s screening programme is largely based on a screen-and-treat strategy using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) followed by cryotherapy or thermoablation. Despite nationwide roll-out, screening coverage remains low and inequitable. The World Health Organization (WHO) now recommends high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) DNA testing – which demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy as opposed to VIA – as the preferred screening method. Emerging point-of-care (POC) HPV tests and self-sampling modalities have shown potential to transform screening accessibility in low-resource settings such as Malawi. This thesis explores the feasibility of integrating POC HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into the Malawian cervical cancer screening programme. Objectives: This work had five main aims: (1) to describe the uptake of cervical cancer screening in Malawi; (2) to quantify and describe the short-term impact of Cyclone Freddy on maternal and reproductive health service utilisation; (3) to evaluate the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing within a screen-and-treat framework; (4) to explore the acceptability of cervical self-sampling among women; and (5) to assess the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting. Findings: Cervical cancer screening coverage in Malawi remains low and uneven, disproportionately favouring HIV-positive and urban women. Climatic shocks, including Cyclone Freddy, disrupted access to essential reproductive health services. Among women screened in rural southern Malawi, HR-HPV prevalence was high and substantial diagnostic discordance existed between VIA and HPV DNA testing. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, with women citing privacy, comfort, and autonomy as key advantages, and HPV rapid testing was demonstrated to be operationally feasible. Implications: These findings highlight the limitations of VIA-based screening and support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing. Integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling could increase coverage, enhance equity, and improve early detection, particularly in rural and climate-vulnerable settings. The results have directly informed the 2024 Malawi National Cancer Treatment Guidelines and provide actionable evidence for policy, training, and scale-up strategies. Future research should evaluate longitudinal outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and implementation pathways to ensure sustainable, resilient, and woman-centred cervical cancer prevention in Malawi.

It also explored the acceptability of self-sampling among women and assessed the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting.
analysis.main_results: Cervical cancer screening coverage in Malawi remains low and uneven, disproportionately favoring HIV-positive and urban women. analysis.summary_en: This study examines the feasibility of integrating point-of-care HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into Malawi's cervical cancer screening program. It highlights the limitations of the current VIA-based approach and the potential of HPV testing to improve coverage and equity. The research demonstrates that self-sampling is highly acceptable and that POC HPV testing is operationally feasible in rural areas. These findings support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing and have informed national guidelines. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit its depth. The evidence suggests a moderate confidence in the feasibility of these interventions in low-resource settings.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Cervical cancer remains a significant public health issue in Malawi, with high incidence and mortality rates despite existing screening programs. The study aimed to explore the feasibility of integrating point-of-care HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into the Malawian cervical cancer screening program.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the Malawian cervical cancer screening program, which primarily uses visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) followed by cryotherapy or thermoablation. It examined the impact of Cyclone Freddy on maternal and reproductive health service utilization and assessed the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing in rural southern Malawi.
analysis_en.methods: The study described the uptake of cervical cancer screening in Malawi, quantified the short-term impact of Cyclone Freddy on health service utilization, and evaluated the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing within a screen-and-treat framework. It also explored the acceptability of self-sampling among women and assessed the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting.
analysis_en.main_results: Cervical cancer screening coverage in Malawi remains low and uneven, disproportionately favoring HIV-positive and urban women. Climatic shocks, including Cyclone Freddy, disrupted access to essential reproductive health services. Among women screened in rural southern Malawi, HR-HPV prevalence was high, and substantial diagnostic discordance existed between VIA and HPV DNA testing. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, with women citing privacy, comfort, and autonomy as key advantages, and HPV rapid testing was demonstrated to be operationally feasible.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the limitations of VIA-based screening and support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing. The study demonstrates that integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling could increase coverage, enhance equity, and improve early detection, particularly in rural and climate-vulnerable settings.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results have directly informed the 2024 Malawi National Cancer Treatment Guidelines and provide actionable evidence for policy, training, and scale-up strategies. Future research should evaluate longitudinal outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and implementation pathways to ensure sustainable, resilient, and woman-centred cervical cancer prevention in Malawi.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on an abstract-only analysis, which may limit the depth of understanding. However, the evidence is sufficient to support the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting, with a moderate confidence level.

papers.title_zh: 了解使用自采样技术和护理点诊断在马拉维筛查 人乳头瘤病毒 的 人乳头瘤病毒 测试的实施和扩大
papers.source_body_en: Background: Although cervical cancer is one of the most preventable malignancies worldwide, Malawi remains among the top five countries globally with the highest incidence and mortality rates from cervical cancer. The country’s screening programme is largely based on a screen-and-treat strategy using visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) followed by cryotherapy or thermoablation. Despite nationwide roll-out, screening coverage remains low and inequitable. The World Health Organization (WHO) now recommends high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) DNA testing – which demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy as opposed to VIA – as the preferred screening method. Emerging point-of-care (POC) HPV tests and self-sampling modalities have shown potential to transform screening accessibility in low-resource settings such as Malawi. This thesis explores the feasibility of integrating POC HPV DNA testing and self-sampling into the Malawian cervical cancer screening programme. Objectives: This work had five main aims: (1) to describe the uptake of cervical cancer screening in Malawi; (2) to quantify and describe the short-term impact of Cyclone Freddy on maternal and reproductive health service utilisation; (3) to evaluate the diagnostic performance of near-POC HR-HPV testing within a screen-and-treat framework; (4) to explore the acceptability of cervical self-sampling among women; and (5) to assess the feasibility of integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling in a low-resource setting. Findings: Cervical cancer screening coverage in Malawi remains low and uneven, disproportionately favouring HIV-positive and urban women. Climatic shocks, including Cyclone Freddy, disrupted access to essential reproductive health services. Among women screened in rural southern Malawi, HR-HPV prevalence was high and substantial diagnostic discordance existed between VIA and HPV DNA testing. Self-sampling was highly acceptable, with women citing privacy, comfort, and autonomy as key advantages, and HPV rapid testing was demonstrated to be operationally feasible. Implications: These findings highlight the limitations of VIA-based screening and support WHO recommendations for transitioning to primary HPV testing. Integrating POC HPV testing with self-sampling could increase coverage, enhance equity, and improve early detection, particularly in rural and climate-vulnerable settings. The results have directly informed the 2024 Malawi National Cancer Treatment Guidelines and provide actionable evidence for policy, training, and scale-up strategies. Future research should evaluate longitudinal outcomes, cost-effectiveness, and implementation pathways to ensure sustainable, resilient, and woman-centred cervical cancer prevention in Malawi.

papers.title: INFLUÊNCIA DA MICROBIOTA VAGINAL NA PERSISTÊNCIA DA INFECÇÃO PELO HPV E NA PROGRESSÃO DAS LESÕES CERVICAIS: UMA REVISÃO DA LITERATURA INFLUENCE OF VAGINAL MICROBIOTA ON HPV INFECTION PERSISTENCE AND CERVICAL LESION PROGRESSION: A LITERATURE REVIEW
papers.abstract: A infecção pelo papilomavírus humano (HPV), especialmente pelos tipos de alto risco, está relacionada ao desenvolvimento de lesões intraepiteliais cervicais e ao câncer de colo do útero. Embora a persistência viral seja um dos principais fatores envolvidos nesse processo, evidências recentes indicam que a composição da microbiota vaginal pode estar relacionada à evolução da infecção. Esse artigo buscou analisar a influência da microbiota vaginal na persistência da infecção pelo HPV e na progressão das lesões cervicais. Foi realizada uma revisão da literatura nas bases PubMed e Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde (BVS), utilizando os descritores “Microbiota”, “Papillomavirus Infections” e “Uterine Cervical Dysplasia”, combinados pelo operador booleano AND. Foram selecionados 25 estudos publicados nos últimos cinco anos, disponíveis gratuitamente e em texto completo. Os resultados demonstraram associação entre disbiose cervicovaginal, alterações na composição de espécies de Lactobacillus e persistência do HPV, além de relações com diferentes graus de lesão cervical. Também foram observadas alterações em bactérias anaeróbias e em perfis metabólicos relacionados à resposta imune local. Conclui-se que a microbiota vaginal pode participar do microambiente associado à persistência do HPV e à progressão das lesões, embora a relação causal ainda não esteja completamente estabelecida.
papers.journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the influence of vaginal microbiota on HPV infection persistence and cervical lesion progression. It highlights the association between vaginal dysbiosis, changes in Lactobacillus species composition, and HPV persistence, as well as links to varying degrees of cervical lesions. Alterations in anaerobic bacteria and metabolic profiles related to local immune response were also observed. While the role of vaginal microbiota in shaping the microenvironment for HPV persistence and lesion progression is suggested, a causal relationship remains unestablished. The review underscores the need for further research to clarify mechanisms and therapeutic implications.

papers.title: Epidemiological profile of HPV infection, associations with cervical lesions and vaginal microecological disorders, and nine-valent vaccine coverage in Northwest China: a 6-year retrospective study of 57,035 women
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer is a leading cause of female cancer mortality globally, with a rising burden in China. Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the established driver of cervical carcinogenesis, but regional epidemiological data and associations between HPV and vaginal microecological disorders remain poorly characterized in Northwest China. We conducted a retrospective study of 57,035 female outpatients at a tertiary hospital in Shaanxi Province from 2016 to 2021. HPV genotyping was performed to assess persistent infection patterns, 9-valent vaccine coverage across three cervical lesion risk strata, and correlations with bacterial vaginosis (BV), aerobic vaginitis (AV), trichomonal vaginitis (TV), and vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC). In this study of 57,035 female outpatients undergoing HPV genotyping, the overall HPV positivity rate was 28.77%, with infections dominated by isolated high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) and single-genotype patterns. HPV16, 52, 58, 53 and 51 were the most prevalent HR-HPV genotypes, and HPV prevalence showed a bimodal age distribution peaking at 26–30 years with a secondary peak at ≥ 61 years. Among 3,542 patients with follow-up, the overall persistent infection rate was 33.75%, highest in mixed HR/LR-HPV infections. HPV positivity correlated with elevated abnormal TCT rates, and nine HR-HPV genotypes were significantly associated with cytological abnormalities; HPV16 accounted for 69.7% of cervical cancer cases. The coverage of 9-valent vaccine genotypes increased with disease severity. HPV infection was positively associated with bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis and mixed vaginitis, but inversely linked to vulvovaginal candidiasis, with subtype-specific association patterns. This study provides comprehensive regional HPV epidemiological evidence and reveals subtype-specific HPV-vaginal microecology interactions, supporting tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies in Northwest China.

papers.title: Regulation and function of the HPV16 CircE7 RNA
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT High-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV), including HPV16, produce circular RNA that encompasses the E7 oncogene (circE7). CircE7 can be detected in HPV16-positive cells and tumors, is preferentially localized to the cytoplasm, is N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A)-modified, and can be translated into the E7 oncoprotein. Here, we explored the regulation and function of circE7. Mutation of m 6 A motifs flanking the backsplice junction revealed a single m 6 A motif to be essential for circE7 formation. Mutation of this m 6 A motif promoted linear splicing of the E6*I splice site (226^409), suggesting that linear and circular E7 splicing are inversely regulated. Additionally, mutation of an IRES-like motif in circE7 significantly decreased E7 protein expression, without having significant effects on circE7 RNA levels. Knockdown of YTHDC1, but not other m 6 A-binding proteins, decreased both circE7 RNA and protein expression. BaseScope ISH was used to confirm the expression of circE7 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cell lines and tumors. Using both qRT-PCR and BaseScope ISH, we found that serum and amino acid starvation significantly increased circE7. Finally, we generated an HPV16 genome with mutations in the circE7 m 6 A motif (Mut2). Stable transduction of primary keratinocytes with Mut2 confirmed the loss of circE7 and increased expression of E6*I. The Mut2 HPV16 genome exhibited significantly decreased viral replication but an increased ability to transform primary keratinocytes. Our studies reveal that the precise regulation of circE7 and E6*I by m 6 A is critical for the ability of HPV16 to infect and transform keratinocytes. IMPORTANCE High-risk human papillomaviruses (HPVs), such as HPV16, must carefully control how much E6 and E7 proteins they make. This study shows that HPV16 toggles a single chemical tag on the viral RNA (an m6A mark) to control the production of early region RNAs, including a circular RNA called circE7. The same site coordinately regulates splicing of the E6*I isoform. CircE7 uses m6A-binding proteins to control its production and a specific sequence to promote its translation. It is present in HPV-positive cancers and can respond to nutrient starvation. Regulation of circE7 through this m 6 A site also impacted viral replication and transformation capacity, indicating that this regulatory mechanism is critical for HPV biology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the regulation and function of circE7 RNA produced by HPV16, as high-risk HPVs, including HPV16, must carefully control how much E6 and E7 proteins they make. The research addresses a knowledge gap regarding the role of circE7 in HPV biology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study explored the regulation and function of circE7 RNA in HPV16-positive cells and tumors, using both in vitro and in vivo models. It involved primary keratinocytes and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cell lines.
analysis.methods: The researchers used qRT-PCR and BaseScope ISH to detect circE7 RNA and its expression. They also performed mutation analyses of m6A motifs and an IRES-like motif in circE7, and conducted stable transduction experiments with a modified HPV16 genome.
analysis.main_results: Mutation of the m6A motif flanking the backsplice junction was found to be essential for circE7 formation. Additionally, mutation of an IRES-like motif in circE7 significantly decreased E7 protein expression, without affecting circE7 RNA levels. Knockdown of YTHDC1, but not other m6A-binding proteins, decreased both circE7 RNA and protein expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the regulation of circE7 and E6*I by m6A is critical for HPV16's ability to infect and transform keratinocytes, highlighting a novel mechanism of viral RNA regulation that impacts both replication and oncogenic potential.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms of HPV16 infection and transformation, which could inform future research on HPV-associated cancers and the development of targeted therapies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on in vitro and in vivo experiments, which may not fully represent the complexity of human HPV infection. The evidence is moderate, as the results are derived from controlled laboratory settings and not from clinical trials.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the regulation and function of circE7 RNA in HPV16, revealing that m6A modification is essential for circE7 formation and that its regulation impacts viral replication and transformation capacity. The research highlights the importance of circE7 in HPV biology and suggests potential therapeutic targets for HPV-associated cancers. However, the findings are based on controlled laboratory experiments, which may limit their generalizability to clinical settings.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用体外和体内模型探索了 circE7 RNA 在 HPV16 阳性细胞和肿瘤中的调节和功能。它涉及原代角质形成细胞和头颈鳞状细胞癌细胞系。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用 qRT-PCR 和 BaseScope ISH 检测 circE7 RNA 及其表达。他们还对 circE7 中的 m6A 基序和 IRES 样基序进行了 突变 分析,并使用修饰的 HPV16 基因组 进行了稳定转导实验。
elements_zh.main_results: 发现背剪接点侧翼的 m6A 基序的 突变 对于 circE7 的形成至关重要。此外,circE7 中 IRES 样基序的 突变 显着降低了 E7 蛋白表达,而不影响 circE7 RNA 水平。YTHDC1 的敲低(而非其他 m6A 结合蛋白)降低了 circE7 RNA 和蛋白质的表达。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,m6A 对 circE7 和 E6*I 的调节对于 HPV16 感染和转化角质形成细胞的能力至关重要,强调了一种影响复制和致癌潜力的病毒 RNA 调节新机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了对 HPV16 感染和转化的分子机制的见解,这可以为未来有关 HPV 相关癌症的研究和靶向治疗的开发提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于体外和体内实验,可能无法完全代表人类HPV感染的复杂性。证据是中等的,因为结果来自受控实验室设置而不是临床试验。

papers.title: Acceptability and preference of self-collected vaginal samples for human papillomavirus DNA testing compared with physician-collected Pap smear.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-collected vaginal sampling for human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA testing provides a promising alternative to physician-collected Pap smears, especially in low-resource settings. However, data on its acceptability and preferences among Filipino women remain limited. This study aimed to assess women's perceptions, experiences, willingness and preferences regarding self-collected vaginal sampling for HPV DNA testing compared with Pap smears. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 592 women. Participants underwent both physician-collected Pap smears and self-collected vaginal sampling for HPV DNA testing. Perceptions were measured using five-point Likert scale questionnaires before and after self-collection. Descriptive statistics were used, and paired and independent Wilcoxon tests were used to compare Likert responses. Willingness to undergo screening was analyzed with Cochran's Q and McNemar tests. Participants' reasons for their preferred screening method were categorized thematically and displayed in stacked bar charts. RESULTS: Self-collection was generally viewed as painless, not uncomfortable, non-embarrassing, and easy and convenient. Acceptability significantly increased after participants performed self-collection (P < 0.001 for pain and discomfort). Compared with Pap smears, self-collection was seen as less embarrassing (P < 0.001), but rated as less easy (P = 0.01) and less convenient (P = 0.004). Most participants preferred physician-administered screening (84.8%) due to trust in medical expertise, and confidence in the procedure's accuracy, safety and cleanliness. CONCLUSIONS: Self-collected vaginal sampling was highly acceptable, yet physician-collected screening remained the preferred method. Improving education, demonstrations, and support for self-collection may enhance the uptake of HPV DNA testing and broaden access to cervical cancer screening in the Philippines.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 自我采集阴道样本用于人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)DNA检测为医生采集的巴氏涂片提供了一种有前景的替代方案,特别是在资源匮乏的环境中。然而,关于菲律宾女性对其可接受性和偏好的数据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在592名女性中进行了一项横断面研究。参与者接受了医生采集的巴氏涂片和自我采集的阴道样本用于HPV DNA检测。
elements_zh.methods: 感知通过五点李克特量表问卷在自我采样前和后进行测量。使用描述性统计,并采用配对和独立样本威尔科克森检验来比较李克特量表的回答。接受筛查的意愿通过科克兰Q检验和麦克纳马检验进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 自我采集通常被认为无痛、不不适、不尴尬且容易和方便。参与者进行自我采集后,可接受性显著提高(疼痛和不适的P < 0.001)。与巴氏涂片相比,自我采集被认为更不尴尬(P < 0.001),但被认为更不便于操作(P = 0.01)和更不方便(P = 0.004)。大多数参与者由于对医疗专业知识的信任以及对程序准确性、安全性和清洁度的信心,更倾向于医生进行的筛查(84.8%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 自我采集阴道样本具有高度可接受性,但医生采集的筛查仍然是首选方法。通过改善自我采集的教育、演示和支持,可能提高HPV DNA检测的参与率,并扩大菲律宾宫颈癌筛查的可及性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可能通过强调自我采样方法的教育和支持需求,为提高菲律宾HPV DNA检测的接受度并扩大筛查可及性提供策略依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于菲律宾的单一人群,并未考虑长期行为变化。证据是温和的,因为它是基于自我报告的看法和经验。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:自我采集阴道样本用于人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)DNA检测为医生采集的巴氏涂片提供了一种有前景的替代方案,特别是在资源匮乏的环境中。然而,关于菲律宾女性对其可接受性和偏好的数据仍然有限。本研究旨在评估女性对自我采集阴道样本进行HPV DNA检测与巴氏涂片的感知、体验、意愿和偏好。方法:在592名女性中进行了一项横断面研究。参与者接受了医生采集的巴氏涂片和自我采集的阴道样本用于HPV DNA检测。使用五点李克特量表问卷在自我采集前后测量感知。采用描述性统计分析,并使用配对和独立Wilcoxon检验比较李克特量表回答。使用Cochran's Q和McNemar检验分析接受筛查的意愿。参与者偏好的筛查方法的原因被主题分类,并以堆叠条形图显示。结果:自我采集通常被认为无痛、不不适、不尴尬且容易和方便。参与者进行自我采集后,可接受性显著提高(疼痛和不适的P < 0.001)。与巴氏涂片相比,自我采集被认为更不尴尬(P < 0.001),但被认为更不便于操作(P = 0.01)和更不方便(P = 0.004)。大多数参与者由于对医疗专业知识的信任以及对程序准确性、安全性和清洁度的信心,更倾向于医生进行的筛查(84.8%)。结论:自我采集阴道样本具有高度可接受性,但医生采集的筛查仍然是首选方法。通过改善自我采集的教育、演示和支持,可能提高HPV DNA检测的参与率,并扩大菲律宾宫颈癌筛查的可及性。科学与公共卫生意义:这些发现可以为提高HPV DNA检测参与率和扩大菲律宾宫颈癌筛查的可及性提供策略依据,强调了对自我采集方法进行教育和支持的必要性。局限性与证据强度:本研究的局限性在于其横断面设计和自我报告数据,这可能引入偏倚。证据强度中等,因为它提供了关于可接受性和偏好的见解,但并未建立因果关系。

papers.title: Enhanced Paper-Based DNA Adsorption and Point-of-Care Detection of High-Risk Human Papillomaviruses 16 and 18.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer screening in low-resource settings requires molecular diagnostics that integrate rapid DNA extraction with sensitive, low-cost DNA amplification and detection. Here, we present a paper-based DNA detection (PDD) platform that introduces two mechanistic advances for decentralized HPV diagnostics. First, we establish a centrifuge-free DNA isolation strategy based on ethanol-assisted capture of DNA onto cellulose paper to provide high-yield DNA. Second, we introduce a coffee-ring-based fluorescence-sensing mechanism that converts the spatial redistribution of PicoGreen-labeled amplified products into a quantitative readout. We report, for the first time, that acid-pretreated cellulose (APC) paper captures DNA efficiently relative to untreated paper, identifying substrate pH as a critical factor in paper-based DNA extraction. FTIR analysis and zeta potential measurements revealed that APC paper retained DNA efficiently primarily through hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interactions, respectively. Moreover, the mechanism behind the coffee ring-based amplified DNA detection was attributed to the chromatographic and evaporation effects. DNA is quantified using peripheral fluorescence intensity (PFI), enabling robust discrimination between positive and negative reactions. The integrated platform detected HPV16 and HPV18 with a limit of detection of 10 copies μL−1. Clinical evaluation of 52 cervical samples demonstrated 100% specificity for both HPV16 and HPV18, 100% sensitivity for HPV18, and 85.7% sensitivity for HPV16 compared with an IVD-approved real-time PCR assay. By combining mechanistically guided DNA isolation with physics-based spatial DNA detection, this work advances paper-based molecular diagnostics beyond conventional intensity-based assays and provides a simple, inexpensive, and field-deployable strategy for point-of-care detection of HR HPVs.

papers.title: Cervicovaginal lipid mediator profiles during high-risk HPV infection associated with subsequent viral clearance or persistence: an exploratory pilot study
papers.abstract: Background High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, whereas most infections are spontaneously cleared. Although local immune and microbial factors associated with HPV outcomes have been investigated, the contribution of lipid mediators within the cervicovaginal microenvironment remains poorly characterized. Methods Cervicovaginal wash samples from 30 participants in a prospective longitudinal HPV cohort were analyzed by targeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Samples were obtained from HPV-negative women, HPV-positive women who were negative for the relevant HPV type at the subsequent visit (subsequent-clearance group), and HPV-positive women in whom the same HPV type remained detectable at the subsequent visit. Results Six lipid mediators were detected in cervicovaginal wash samples. During HPV infection, women with subsequent clearance had higher measured concentrations of total 12-HETE and total 14-HDHA than HPV-negative women. In the secondary percentage-based analysis, the relative contribution of PGE 2 was lower in the subsequent-clearance group than in both the HPV-negative and subsequent-persistence groups, while the relative contribution of total 14-HDHA was higher in the subsequent-persistence group than in HPV-negative women. Direct comparison of correlation coefficients identified an opposite TxB 2 –14-HDHA relationship in subsequent clearance and persistence. Conclusions Higher cervicovaginal concentrations of total 12-HETE and total 14-HDHA during HPV infection were associated with clearance of the relevant HPV type at the subsequent visit. The opposite TxB 2 –total 14-HDHA associations observed in subsequent clearance and persistence further suggest outcome-associated differences in lipid-mediator coordination. These exploratory findings identify lipid mediators as candidate correlates of HPV outcomes.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results highlight the potential of lipid mediators as biomarkers for predicting HPV infection outcomes, which could inform future studies on surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is exploratory and based on a small sample size, limiting the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to the lack of large-scale validation and the observational nature of the study.

papers.title_zh: 高危型HPV 感染期间的宫颈阴道脂质介质谱与随后的病毒清除或持续性相关:一项探索性试点研究
papers.source_body_en: Background High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is the primary cause of cervical cancer, whereas most infections are spontaneously cleared. Although local immune and microbial factors associated with HPV outcomes have been investigated, the contribution of lipid mediators within the cervicovaginal microenvironment remains poorly characterized. Methods Cervicovaginal wash samples from 30 participants in a prospective longitudinal HPV cohort were analyzed by targeted liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Samples were obtained from HPV-negative women, HPV-positive women who were negative for the relevant HPV type at the subsequent visit (subsequent-clearance group), and HPV-positive women in whom the same HPV type remained detectable at the subsequent visit. Results Six lipid mediators were detected in cervicovaginal wash samples. During HPV infection, women with subsequent clearance had higher measured concentrations of total 12-HETE and total 14-HDHA than HPV-negative women. In the secondary percentage-based analysis, the relative contribution of PGE 2 was lower in the subsequent-clearance group than in both the HPV-negative and subsequent-persistence groups, while the relative contribution of total 14-HDHA was higher in the subsequent-persistence group than in HPV-negative women. Direct comparison of correlation coefficients identified an opposite TxB 2 –14-HDHA relationship in subsequent clearance and persistence. Conclusions Higher cervicovaginal concentrations of total 12-HETE and total 14-HDHA during HPV infection were associated with clearance of the relevant HPV type at the subsequent visit. The opposite TxB 2 –total 14-HDHA associations observed in subsequent clearance and persistence further suggest outcome-associated differences in lipid-mediator coordination. These exploratory findings identify lipid mediators as candidate correlates of HPV outcomes.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景 高危 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染是 宫颈癌 的主要原因,而大多数感染会自行清除。尽管已经研究了与 HPV 结果相关的局部免疫和微生物因素,但宫颈阴道微环境中脂质介质的作用仍知之甚少。方法 采用靶向液相色谱-串联质谱法对前瞻性纵向 HPV 队列研究 中 30 名参与者的宫颈阴道冲洗样本进行分析。样本取自 HPV 阴性女性、在随后就诊时相关 HPV 类型呈阴性的 HPV 阳性女性(后续清除组)以及在随后就诊时仍可检测到相同 HPV 类型的 HPV 阳性女性。结果在宫颈阴道冲洗样品中检测到六种脂质介质。在 HPV 感染期间,随后清除的女性比 HPV 阴性女性测得的总 12-HETE 和总 14-HDHA 浓度更高。在基于百分比的二次分析中,后续清除组中 PGE 2 的相对贡献低于 HPV 阴性组和后续持续组,而后续持续组中总 14-HDHA 的相对贡献高于 HPV 阴性女性。相关系数的直接比较确定了随后的清除率和持久性中相反的 TxB 2 –14-HDHA 关系。结论 HPV 感染期间宫颈阴道总 12-HETE 和总 14-HDHA 浓度较高与后续就诊时相关 HPV 类型的清除相关。在随后的清除和持久性中观察到的相反的 TxB 2 – 总 14-HDHA 关联进一步表明脂质介质协调中与结果相关的差异。这些探索性发现将脂质介质确定为 HPV 结果的候选相关因素。

papers.title: Sexual Health and Well-Being in Women with Human Papillomavirus (HPV): A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: This scoping review aims to map the research on the impact of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection on women's sexual health and sexual well-being. Although HPV is one of the most prevalent sexually transmitted infections worldwide and that most infections are transient and clinically benign, growing evidence suggests that HPV diagnosis, follow-up procedures, and treatment may have significant emotional, psychosocial, relational, and sexual consequences for women. The review is guided by the following overarching research question: What is the nature of the evidence on the sexual health and well-being of women with HPV infection across its clinical trajectory (screening, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up), in relation to emotional, psychosocial, relational, and sexual functioning outcomes? Following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews and the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines, this review includes empirical quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies involving adult women diagnosed with cervical, vaginal, or vulvar HPV infection. Evidence will be mapped across several domains, including emotional responses (e.g., anxiety, fear, shame, distress), psychosocial factors (e.g., stigma, health literacy, self-image, coping), relationship and communication processes, sexual functioning (e.g., desire, arousal, orgasm, pain, satisfaction), and experiences associated with different stages of the HPV clinical pathway. The expected outcomes of this review are to provide a comprehensive overview of current knowledge, identify patterns and gaps in the literature, and support the development of more integrated biopsychosocial approaches to HPV care. The findings may contribute to improving clinical communication, psychosocial support, sexual health interventions, and patient-centred care for women living with HPV.

papers.title: Real-world clinical outcomes of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1
papers.abstract: Background Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1) is generally managed by observation because spontaneous regression is common and progression to high-grade disease is uncommon. Nevertheless, some patients with persistent HPV infection or repeated low-grade abnormalities may elect active treatment after appropriate counseling. This study aimed to describe the clinical outcomes and safety of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) in patients with CIN1 who underwent active treatment. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 269 patients with CIN1 who underwent ALA-PDT at Peking University Shenzhen Hospital between July 2021 and July 2025. All patients received six sessions of ALA-PDT at intervals of 7–14 days. HPV status and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) results were assessed before treatment and during follow-up at 3 months (± 1 month) and, in some patients, at 6 months (± 1 month) after treatment. HPV clearance, cytological improvement, and treatment-related adverse events were analyzed. Results Among the 266 HPV-positive patients, 155 patients (58.27%) had a negative HPV result at the predefined 3-month follow-up. At 3 months, 205 of 247 patients (83.00%) with available cytological assessment had NILM cytology. No serious adverse events were observed during treatment or follow-up. Conclusions In this retrospective cohort study, HPV negativity and improved cytological findings were observed during follow-up after ALA-PDT, together with an acceptable safety profile and no serious adverse events.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the clinical outcomes and safety of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1). The research is motivated by the need for active treatment in some patients with persistent HPV infection or repeated low-grade abnormalities. A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 269 patients treated at Peking University Shenzhen Hospital between July 2021 and July 2025. HPV status and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) results were assessed before and during follow-up. The results showed that 58.27% of HPV-positive patients had negative HPV results at 3 months, and 83.00% had NILM cytology. The authors interpret these findings as indicating HPV clearance and improved cytological outcomes with an acceptable safety profile. The study suggests that ALA-PDT may be a useful treatment for CIN1 patients with persistent HPV infection. However, the study's retrospective design limits the strength of the evidence, which is considered moderate.

papers.source_body_en: Background Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 1 (CIN1) is generally managed by observation because spontaneous regression is common and progression to high-grade disease is uncommon. Nevertheless, some patients with persistent HPV infection or repeated low-grade abnormalities may elect active treatment after appropriate counseling. This study aimed to describe the clinical outcomes and safety of 5-aminolevulinic acid photodynamic therapy (ALA-PDT) in patients with CIN1 who underwent active treatment. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 269 patients with CIN1 who underwent ALA-PDT at Peking University Shenzhen Hospital between July 2021 and July 2025. All patients received six sessions of ALA-PDT at intervals of 7–14 days. HPV status and ThinPrep cytologic test (TCT) results were assessed before treatment and during follow-up at 3 months (± 1 month) and, in some patients, at 6 months (± 1 month) after treatment. HPV clearance, cytological improvement, and treatment-related adverse events were analyzed. Results Among the 266 HPV-positive patients, 155 patients (58.27%) had a negative HPV result at the predefined 3-month follow-up. At 3 months, 205 of 247 patients (83.00%) with available cytological assessment had NILM cytology. No serious adverse events were observed during treatment or follow-up. Conclusions In this retrospective cohort study, HPV negativity and improved cytological findings were observed during follow-up after ALA-PDT, together with an acceptable safety profile and no serious adverse events.

papers.title: owledge and Baseline Awareness of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) as a Potential Factor in Cervical Cancer among Female Adolescents in Secondary Schools in Oyo
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women in Nigeria. Despite the integration of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine into the national immunization schedule to target female adolescents, vaccine hesitancy driven by poor baseline knowledge and suboptimal awareness presents a significant bottleneck to eradication efforts. This cross-sectional school-based study was carried out to assess the baseline awareness and health attitudes regarding HPV among 245 female secondary school adolescents in Oyo State. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, baseline study, and awareness of the link between HPV and cervical cancer were collected using validated, self-administered structured questionnaires. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. The mean age of the participants fell predominantly within the 15–17 years range (62.8%, n=155), and participants were primarily Yoruba (87.4%, n=216). Basic awareness of HPV was low: only 43.3% (n=107) had never heard of the virus, and 56.7% (n=140) had no prior exposure. The internet and social media were the leading information channels (26.7%, n=66), outperforming healthcare workers (17.0%, n=42). Strikingly, 68.0% (n=168) were completely unaware of HPV symptoms, and 58.7% (n=145) confessed total ignorance regarding specific clinical manifestations. Furthermore, while 44.9% (n=111) recognized that HPV causes cervical cancer, only 34.8% (n=84) understood that preventing HPV infection directly reduces cervical cancer risks. Female adolescents in Oyo present deficient public health knowledge and low awareness regarding HPV and its oncogenic links to cervical cancer. Digital landscapes offer the most viable window for intervention.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项以学校为基础的横断面研究旨在评估奥约州 245 名中学女生对 HPV 的基线认识和健康态度。参与者的平均年龄主要在 15-17 岁范围内(62.8%,n=155),参与者主要是约鲁巴人(87.4%,n=216)。
elements_zh.methods: 使用经过验证的、自我管理的结构化问卷收集有关社会人口特征、基线研究以及对 HPV 和 宫颈癌 之间联系的认识的数据。使用描述性统计分析数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 对HPV的基本认知度较低:只有43.3%(n=107)从未听说过该病毒,56.7%(n=140)以前没有接触过该病毒。引人注目的是,68.0% (n=168) 的人完全不知道 HPV 症状,58.7% (n=145) 承认完全不了解具体的临床表现。此外,虽然 44.9% (n=111) 的受访者认识到 HPV 会导致 宫颈癌,但只有 34.8% (n=84) 的受访者了解预防 HPV 感染可直接降低 宫颈癌 风险。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Oyo 的女性青少年对 HPV 及其与 宫颈癌 的致癌联系缺乏公共卫生知识和认识。数字景观提供了最可行的干预窗口。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调,迫切需要采取有针对性的教育干预措施,以提高奥约州女性青少年对 HPV 的认识,这可以提高 疫苗 的吸收率并减少 宫颈癌 发病率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到横截面设计的限制,无法建立因果关系,而且依赖自我报告的数据,可能会引入偏差。证据是中等的,因为它提供了意识的快照,但缺乏纵向或干预数据。

Despite the integration of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine into the national immunization schedule to target female adolescents, vaccine hesitancy driven by poor baseline knowledge and suboptimal awareness presents a significant bottleneck to eradication efforts. This cross-sectional school-based study was carried out to assess the baseline awareness and health attitudes regarding HPV among 245 female secondary school adolescents in Oyo State. Data on socio-demographic characteristics, baseline study, and awareness of the link between HPV and cervical cancer were collected using validated, self-administered structured questionnaires. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. The mean age of the participants fell predominantly within the 15–17 years range (62.8%, n=155), and participants were primarily Yoruba (87.4%, n=216). Basic awareness of HPV was low: only 43.3% (n=107) had never heard of the virus, and 56.7% (n=140) had no prior exposure. The internet and social media were the leading information channels (26.7%, n=66), outperforming healthcare workers (17.0%, n=42). Strikingly, 68.0% (n=168) were completely unaware of HPV symptoms, and 58.7% (n=145) confessed total ignorance regarding specific clinical manifestations. Furthermore, while 44.9% (n=111) recognized that HPV causes cervical cancer, only 34.8% (n=84) understood that preventing HPV infection directly reduces cervical cancer risks. Female adolescents in Oyo present deficient public health knowledge and low awareness regarding HPV and its oncogenic links to cervical cancer. Digital landscapes offer the most viable window for intervention.

papers.title: High-risk factors associated with persistence and progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 in women of reproductive age undergoing conservative management: a retrospective analysis
papers.abstract: Objective To investigate the high-risk factors associated with the persistence or progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 (CIN2) to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 (CIN3) in women of childbearing age undergoing conservative management, thereby providing guidance for selecting appropriate treatment strategies for women with CIN2 who wish to preserve their fertility. Methods Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed using the clinical and pathological characteristics of the included patients to identify high-risk factors associated with the persistence or progression of CIN2. Results In total, 226 patients were included in this study. Of these, 142 (62.8%) experienced lesion regression, 58 (25.7%) had persistent CIN2, and 26 (11.5%) progressed to CIN3. Univariate analysis indicated that age, high- squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), human papillomavirus type 16/18 (HPV16/18) positivity, and P16/Ki-67 positivity were associated with persistence of CIN2 or progression to CIN3. Multivariate analysis revealed that age of >35 years (OR 2.732, 95% CI 1.350–5.529), HPV16/18 positivity (OR 1.506, 95% CI 1.129–17.611), HSIL (OR 4.693, 95% CI 3.554–19.211), and P16/Ki-67 positivity (OR 4.007, 95% CI 2.819–6.014) were associated with persistence or progression of CIN2. Conclusion Age of >35 years, HPV16/18 positivity, HSIL, and P16/Ki-67 positivity are associated with persistence and progression of CIN2. Conservative management with outpatient follow-up is an appropriate treatment option for carefully selected patients without these high-risk factors.

papers.title_zh: 与接受保守治疗的育龄妇女宫颈上皮内瘤变2持续存在和进展相关的高危因素:回顾性分析
papers.source_body_en: Objective To investigate the high-risk factors associated with the persistence or progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 (CIN2) to cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 3 (CIN3) in women of childbearing age undergoing conservative management, thereby providing guidance for selecting appropriate treatment strategies for women with CIN2 who wish to preserve their fertility. Methods Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed using the clinical and pathological characteristics of the included patients to identify high-risk factors associated with the persistence or progression of CIN2. Results In total, 226 patients were included in this study. Of these, 142 (62.8%) experienced lesion regression, 58 (25.7%) had persistent CIN2, and 26 (11.5%) progressed to CIN3. Univariate analysis indicated that age, high- squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL), human papillomavirus type 16/18 (HPV16/18) positivity, and P16/Ki-67 positivity were associated with persistence of CIN2 or progression to CIN3. Multivariate analysis revealed that age of >35 years (OR 2.732, 95% CI 1.350–5.529), HPV16/18 positivity (OR 1.506, 95% CI 1.129–17.611), HSIL (OR 4.693, 95% CI 3.554–19.211), and P16/Ki-67 positivity (OR 4.007, 95% CI 2.819–6.014) were associated with persistence or progression of CIN2. Conclusion Age of >35 years, HPV16/18 positivity, HSIL, and P16/Ki-67 positivity are associated with persistence and progression of CIN2. Conservative management with outpatient follow-up is an appropriate treatment option for carefully selected patients without these high-risk factors.

papers.title: Ubiquitin-specific proteases and the immune microenvironment in cervical cancer: mechanistic evidence, immunotherapy resistance, and therapeutic perspectives.
papers.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health burden, and resistance limits the benefit of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Ubiquitin-specific proteases (USPs) regulate protein homeostasis and may connect human papillomavirus-associated oncogenesis with immune evasion. This narrative review evaluates USP-dependent mechanisms relevant to cervical cancer, distinguishing disease-specific findings from evidence in other tumor types and proposed pathways. Cervical cancer studies support USP7-associated immune-checkpoint regulation and USP14-dependent MCT4 stabilization and lactate export, although the immune consequences of the latter remain inferred. Evidence linking USPs to regulatory T-cell function, STING signaling, antigen presentation, and immunosuppressive metabolism derives largely from non-cervical experimental systems. The proposed E6-USP7 and E7-USP1 immune pathways therefore require direct validation. We discuss small-molecule inhibitors, targeted protein degradation and stabilization, combination strategies, and biomarker development. Compensatory USP Reprogramming (CUR) and a proposed USP-based tumor immune microenvironment (USP-TIME) framework are presented as hypotheses for investigating treatment-associated adaptation and the relationship between USP profiles and immune architecture, respectively. Therapeutic development must account for the possibility that USP inhibition also impairs antigen presentation or effector lymphocyte function. papers.abstract_zh: 宫颈癌 仍然是全球主要的健康负担,耐药性限制了免疫检查点抑制剂 (ICIs) 的益处。泛素特异性蛋白酶 (USP) 调节蛋白质稳态,并可能将 人乳头瘤病毒 相关的肿瘤发生与免疫逃避联系起来。这篇叙述性综述评估了与 宫颈癌 相关的 USP 依赖性机制,将疾病特异性发现与其他肿瘤类型的证据和拟议的途径区分开来。宫颈癌 研究支持 USP7 相关的免疫检查点调节以及 USP14 依赖的 MCT4 稳定和乳酸输出,尽管后者的免疫后果仍然存在推断。将 USP 与调节性 T 细胞功能、STING 信号传导、抗原呈递和免疫抑制代谢联系起来的证据主要来自非宫颈实验系统。因此,所提出的 E6-USP7 和 E7-USP1 免疫途径需要直接验证。我们讨论小分子抑制剂、靶向蛋白质降解和稳定、组合策略和生物标志物开发。补偿性 USP 重编程 (CUR) 和提出的基于 USP 的肿瘤免疫微环境 (USP-TIME) 框架分别作为研究 治疗 相关适应以及 USP 谱与免疫结构之间关系的假设。治疗开发必须考虑到 USP 抑制也会损害抗原呈递或效应淋巴细胞功能的可能性。尽管 USP 指导的方法为进一步研究提供了理由,但它们在 宫颈癌 中的临床益处尚未得到证实。进展需要细胞类型解析的机制研究、免疫活性模型、经过验证的药效学分析和化合物特异性安全评估。

papers.title: Neurological Complications of Oncogenic Viruses: Mechanisms, Clinical Manifestations, and Emerging Insights.
papers.abstract: Oncogenic viruses are widely recognized for their pivotal role in malignant transformation; however, their capacity to induce neurological disorders has received comparatively less attention. Increasing evidence indicates that several oncogenic viruses, including human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), are associated with a broad spectrum of neurological complications involving both the central and peripheral nervous systems. These manifestations arise through diverse mechanisms, including direct viral neuroinvasion, persistent infection, immune-mediated tissue injury, chronic neuroinflammation, and disruption of neurovascular integrity. Moreover, virus-induced molecular alterations, such as oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodelling, and aberrant cytokine signalling, contribute t neuronal dysfunction and disease progression. In this review, we critically examine the current understanding of the neurological complications associated with major oncogenic viruses by integrating evidence from molecular, experimental, and clinical studies. We first discuss the general mechanisms by which viral infections induce neurological injury, highlighting pathways shared among neurotropic and non-neurotropic viruses. We then summarise the neurological manifestations and virus-specific pathogenic mechanisms associated with each oncogenic virus, emphasising both common and distinct molecular pathways underlying neuropathogenesis. Finally, we address current diagnostic challenges, emerging biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies while identifying critical knowledge gaps that limit causal interpretation and clinical translation. A comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions between oncogenic viruses, the immune system, and the nervous system will facilitate earlier diagnosis, improve patient management, and support the development of targeted therapeutic approaches for virus-associated neurological disorders.

papers.title_zh: 致癌病毒的神经并发症:机制、临床表现和新见解。
papers.source_body_en: Oncogenic viruses are widely recognized for their pivotal role in malignant transformation; however, their capacity to induce neurological disorders has received comparatively less attention. papers.abstract_zh: 致癌病毒因其在恶性转化中的关键作用而被广泛认可。然而,它们引起神经系统疾病的能力相对较少受到关注。越来越多的证据表明,多种致癌病毒,包括人类 T 细胞白血病病毒 1 型 (HTLV-1)、人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV)、乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV)、丙型肝炎病毒 (HCV) 和卡波西肉瘤相关疱疹病毒 (KSHV),与涉及中枢和周围神经系统的广泛神经系统并发症有关。这些表现是通过多种机制产生的,包括直接病毒神经侵袭、持续感染、免疫介导的组织损伤、慢性神经炎症和神经血管完整性破坏。此外,病毒诱导的分子改变,如氧化应激、线粒体功能障碍、表观遗传重塑和异常的细胞因子信号传导,会导致神经元功能障碍和疾病进展。在这篇综述中,我们通过整合分子、实验和临床研究的证据,批判性地研究了目前对与主要致癌病毒相关的神经并发症的理解。我们首先讨论病毒感染引起神经损伤的一般机制,强调嗜神经病毒和非嗜神经病毒之间共享的途径。然后,我们总结了与每种致癌病毒相关的神经学表现和病毒特异性致病机制,强调神经发病机制中常见和独特的分子途径。最后,我们解决当前的诊断挑战、新兴生物标志物和治疗策略,同时确定限制因果解释和临床转化的关键知识差距。全面了解致癌病毒、免疫系统和神经系统之间复杂的相互作用将有助于早期 诊断,改善患者管理,并支持开发针对病毒相关神经系统疾病的靶向治疗方法。

papers.title: Detection of circulating tumor HPV-DNA in patients with HPV-positive sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Approximately 30% of sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma cases are HPV-associated, yet studies investigating circulating tumor HPV-DNA (ctHPV-DNA) among these patients are scarce. The aim of this study was to investigate the sensitivity of ctHPV-DNA in pretreatment blood samples from patients with HPV-positive (HPV+) sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. METHODS: Patients with a confirmed HPV+ sinonasal or nasopharyngeal carcinoma treated at the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology at Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark in the period 2017-2025 were included in this study. Blood samples were drawn in Streck tubes before treatment initiation and analysed for the presence of ctHPV-DNA by Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). RESULTS: Fifteen patients with primary HPV+ sinonasal or nasopharyngeal carcinoma were included. Except for two cases of HPV-related multiphenotypic carcinoma, all cases were squamous cell carcinoma. HPV16 was most prevalent and found in 6 patients (40%). HPV18 (n = 2), HPV33 (n = 1), HPV35 (n = 3), HPV45 (n = 1), and HPV56 (n = 2) were also represented. The sensitivity of detecting ctHPV-DNA in the pretreatment blood samples of the included patients was 80%. The level of ctHPV-DNA increased significantly with increasing T-category. CONCLUSION: ctHPV-DNA was detected in pretreatment blood samples in 80% of patients with HPV+ sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. This supports further investigation of ctHPV-DNA as a biomarker for post-treatment surveillance in these patients.

papers.title_zh: HPV阳性鼻咽癌患者循环肿瘤HPV-DNA检测
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Approximately 30% of sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma cases are HPV-associated, yet studies investigating circulating tumor HPV-DNA (ctHPV-DNA) among these patients are scarce. The aim of this study was to investigate the sensitivity of ctHPV-DNA in pretreatment blood samples from patients with HPV-positive (HPV+) sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. METHODS: Patients with a confirmed HPV+ sinonasal or nasopharyngeal carcinoma treated at the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology at Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark in the period 2017-2025 were included in this study. Blood samples were drawn in Streck tubes before treatment initiation and analysed for the presence of ctHPV-DNA by Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). RESULTS: Fifteen patients with primary HPV+ sinonasal or nasopharyngeal carcinoma were included. Except for two cases of HPV-related multiphenotypic carcinoma, all cases were squamous cell carcinoma. HPV16 was most prevalent and found in 6 patients (40%). HPV18 (n = 2), HPV33 (n = 1), HPV35 (n = 3), HPV45 (n = 1), and HPV56 (n = 2) were also represented. The sensitivity of detecting ctHPV-DNA in the pretreatment blood samples of the included patients was 80%. The level of ctHPV-DNA increased significantly with increasing T-category. CONCLUSION: ctHPV-DNA was detected in pretreatment blood samples in 80% of patients with HPV+ sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. This supports further investigation of ctHPV-DNA as a biomarker for post-treatment surveillance in these patients.

papers.title: Understanding HPV in Men: A Review of the Prevalence, Risk Factors, Health Outcomes, Transmission, Diagnostics, and Vaccination Strategies
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted viral infection worldwide, with an estimated 630 million people currently infected, and poses significant health risks for men. While many will naturally clear the infection within a couple of years, persistent cancerous HPV strains are linked to several oncological diseases. The aim is to synthesize existing research on HPV in men to better understand its prevalence, risk factors, associated health outcomes, transmission dynamics, diagnostics, and vaccination strategies. Methods: A non-systematic narrative review was conducted, utilizing relevant studies published between 2010 and 2025 identified using multiple databases (Web of Science, PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar) and official health/vaccine websites. Results: Approximately one-third of men globally carry genital HPV, and approximately one-fifth carry one or more high-risk HPV types. Prevalence peaks in younger men but remains high throughout all ages. Key risk factors include sexual behavior, circumcision status, condom use, HIV, smoking, lower education, and vaccination status. More than 80% of infections are asymptomatic, and many men remain unaware due to lack of recommended screening. Emerging strategies focus on high-risk groups, using anal Pap smears and HPV DNA testing. Vaccination in males shows high efficacy, especially when administered before exposure, supporting expanded vaccination programs for all genders. However, global HPV vaccination coverage in men remains suboptimal. Strategies to improve uptake include provider recommendations, education, tailored campaigns, school programs, reminder systems, cost reduction, catch-up vaccination, and open communication. Conclusions: Expanding male-targeted prevention is critical to reducing the global burden of HPV-related diseases.

papers.source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted viral infection worldwide, with an estimated 630 million people currently infected, and poses significant health risks for men. While many will naturally clear the infection within a couple of years, persistent cancerous HPV strains are linked to several oncological diseases. The aim is to synthesize existing research on HPV in men to better understand its prevalence, risk factors, associated health outcomes, transmission dynamics, diagnostics, and vaccination strategies. Methods: A non-systematic narrative review was conducted, utilizing relevant studies published between 2010 and 2025 identified using multiple databases (Web of Science, PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar) and official health/vaccine websites. Results: Approximately one-third of men globally carry genital HPV, and approximately one-fifth carry one or more high-risk HPV types. Prevalence peaks in younger men but remains high throughout all ages. Key risk factors include sexual behavior, circumcision status, condom use, HIV, smoking, lower education, and vaccination status. More than 80% of infections are asymptomatic, and many men remain unaware due to lack of recommended screening. Emerging strategies focus on high-risk groups, using anal Pap smears and HPV DNA testing. Vaccination in males shows high efficacy, especially when administered before exposure, supporting expanded vaccination programs for all genders. However, global HPV vaccination coverage in men remains suboptimal. Strategies to improve uptake include provider recommendations, education, tailored campaigns, school programs, reminder systems, cost reduction, catch-up vaccination, and open communication. Conclusions: Expanding male-targeted prevention is critical to reducing the global burden of HPV-related diseases.

papers.title: Systems Pharmacology of Human Oncoviruses: Network-Based Drug Discovery for Virus-Driven Cancers.
papers.abstract: Human oncoviruses, including high-risk HPV, EBV, HBV, HCV, MCPyV, KSHV, and HTLV-1, account for approximately 15%-20% of global human malignancies. Rather than acting through isolated pathways, viral oncoproteins systematically rewire host regulatory networks, rendering conventional single-target oncology paradigms vulnerable to rapid resistance and clinical failure. Systems pharmacology offers a transformative, network-centric framework that views virus-driven cancers as systemic perturbations of host protein-protein interaction networks. This review synthesises computational methodology, network topology, and drug discovery strategies across major human oncoviruses. We examine how graph centrality algorithms, quantitative network proximity metrics (Z-score), and complementary exposure synergy modelling (S AB ) uncover hidden network vulnerabilities and guide targeted drug repurposing. Despite distinct genomic structures and tissue tropisms, oncogenic viruses converge on shared host interactome hubs, notably TP53, AKT1, BCL2, MYC, STAT3, and VEGFA, to drive cell cycle dysregulation, apoptotic suppression, and microenvironmental remodelling. We evaluate repositioned synthetic pharmaceuticals (such as kinase inhibitors and host ion channel blockers) and multi-target bioactive formulations, detailing their mechanisms in targeting viral host dependencies. Finally, we address key translational bottlenecks, including disparities between in silico binding predictions and in vivo pharmacokinetics, extensive plasma protein binding, tumour penetration barriers, and viral latency reservoirs. Overcoming these hurdles will require integrating deep graph learning, single-cell spatial multi-omics, and patient-derived organoid models to accelerate the clinical realization of network-targeted therapies in viral oncology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This review addresses the need for a more comprehensive understanding of how human oncoviruses, particularly high-risk HPV, contribute to global malignancies and the limitations of conventional single-target oncology approaches in treating virus-driven cancers.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of computational methodologies and drug discovery strategies focused on major human oncoviruses, including high-risk HPV, and their interactions with host networks.
analysis.methods: The review employs graph centrality algorithms, quantitative network proximity metrics (Z-score), and complementary exposure synergy modelling (S AB ) to identify network vulnerabilities and guide targeted drug repurposing for virus-driven cancers.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights that oncogenic viruses, including high-risk HPV, converge on shared host interactome hubs such as TP53, AKT1, BCL2, MYC, STAT3, and VEGFA, which are critical for cell cycle dysregulation, apoptotic suppression, and microenvironmental remodelling.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the convergence of oncogenic viruses on shared host hubs suggests a common therapeutic target, and they present a novel framework for drug discovery that integrates systems pharmacology and network-based approaches.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of network-targeted therapies for HPV-associated cancers, such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cervical cancer, by identifying shared vulnerabilities in host interactomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a review of existing methodologies and does not present original experimental data, but it provides a high-level synthesis of current approaches with a moderate confidence in their applicability to HPV-driven cancers.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV) in driving malignancies by systematically rewiring host regulatory networks. It presents a novel systems pharmacology framework that identifies shared host interactome hubs, such as TP53 and AKT1, as potential therapeutic targets. The study highlights the convergence of oncogenic viruses on these hubs, suggesting a unified approach to drug discovery for virus-driven cancers. However, the review is limited to existing methodologies and does not include original experimental data. The findings have significant implications for the development of network-based therapies for HPV-associated diseases, including cervical cancer. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of primary data and the reliance on computational models. The review also addresses challenges such as in vivo pharmacokinetics and tumour penetration barriers that must be overcome for clinical translation.

papers.title_zh: 人类肿瘤病毒的系统药理学:针对病毒驱动的癌症的基于网络的药物发现。
papers.source_body_en: Human oncoviruses, including high-risk HPV, EBV, HBV, HCV, MCPyV, KSHV, and HTLV-1, account for approximately 15%-20% of global human malignancies. Rather than acting through isolated pathways, viral oncoproteins systematically rewire host regulatory networks, rendering conventional single-target oncology paradigms vulnerable to rapid resistance and clinical failure. Systems pharmacology offers a transformative, network-centric framework that views virus-driven cancers as systemic perturbations of host protein-protein interaction networks. This review synthesises computational methodology, network topology, and drug discovery strategies across major human oncoviruses. We examine how graph centrality algorithms, quantitative network proximity metrics (Z-score), and complementary exposure synergy modelling (S AB ) uncover hidden network vulnerabilities and guide targeted drug repurposing. Despite distinct genomic structures and tissue tropisms, oncogenic viruses converge on shared host interactome hubs, notably TP53, AKT1, BCL2, MYC, STAT3, and VEGFA, to drive cell cycle dysregulation, apoptotic suppression, and microenvironmental remodelling. We evaluate repositioned synthetic pharmaceuticals (such as kinase inhibitors and host ion channel blockers) and multi-target bioactive formulations, detailing their mechanisms in targeting viral host dependencies. Finally, we address key translational bottlenecks, including disparities between in silico binding predictions and in vivo pharmacokinetics, extensive plasma protein binding, tumour penetration barriers, and viral latency reservoirs. Overcoming these hurdles will require integrating deep graph learning, single-cell spatial multi-omics, and patient-derived organoid models to accelerate the clinical realization of network-targeted therapies in viral oncology.
papers.abstract_zh: 人类肿瘤病毒,包括 高危型HPV、EBV、HBV、HCV、MCPyV、KSHV 和 HTLV-1,约占全球人类恶性肿瘤的 15%-20%。病毒癌蛋白不是通过孤立的途径发挥作用,而是系统地重新连接 宿主 调控网络,使传统的单靶点肿瘤学范例容易受到快速耐药性和临床失败的影响。系统药理学提供了一个变革性的、以网络为中心的框架,将病毒驱动的癌症视为 宿主 蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络的系统性扰动。这篇综述综合了主要人类肿瘤病毒的计算方法、网络拓扑和药物发现策略。我们研究图中心性算法、定量网络邻近度指标(Z 分数)和互补暴露协同模型(SAB)如何发现隐藏的网络漏洞并指导靶向药物的重新利用。尽管具有不同的基因组结构和组织向性,致癌病毒聚集在共享的 宿主 相互作用组中心,特别是 TP53、AKT1、BCL2、MYC、STAT3 和 VEGFA,以驱动细胞周期失调、凋亡抑制和微环境重塑。我们评估重新定位的合成药物(例如激酶抑制剂和 宿主 离子通道阻滞剂)和多靶点生物活性制剂,详细说明其针对病毒 宿主 依赖性的机制。最后,我们解决了关键的翻译瓶颈,包括计算机结合预测和体内药代动力学之间的差异、广泛的血浆蛋白结合、肿瘤渗透障碍和病毒潜伏期 储存宿主。克服这些障碍需要整合深度图学习、单细胞空间多组学和患者衍生的类器官模型,以加速病毒肿瘤学网络靶向治疗的临床实现。

papers.title: Modulation of the FAK-Src Signalling Axis by Oncoviruses: Molecular Mechanisms, Functional Consequences, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Oncoviruses play a role in cellular transformation and cancer progression by manipulating host signalling pathways, such as the FAK-Src axis. Preclinical evidence suggests that viral proteins can modulate this axis through direct interactions, integrin signalling, tumour suppressor inactivation, transcriptional and kinase reprogramming, calcium/ROS signalling, regulation of phosphatases, and epigenetic modifications. Important examples include HPV E2 and E6/E7, EBV LMP1 and LMP2A, HBV HBx, HCV Core and E2, and KSHV proteins. FAK-Src disruption can activate pathways such as PI3K/AKT, Rho GTPase, AP-1, and NF-κB, thereby enhancing migration, invasion, survival, angiogenesis, and modulation of the immune response. In some infections, this axis may also be involved at different stages of the viral life cycle. This review examines the molecular mechanisms of FAK-Src regulation by oncoviruses and its functional and therapeutic implications. It also reviews FAK/Src targeting strategies, distinguishing experimental inhibitors, multitargeted agents, and compounds under clinical evaluation, emphasising the limited clinical evidence specific to each virus. Finally, pFAK and pSrc are reviewed as potential markers of pathway activation and pharmacodynamic interaction with the target; however, current evidence is insufficient for their use as valid diagnostic or predictive biomarkers. A better understanding of the virus-host-FAK/Src interaction could help develop mechanism-based therapeutic approaches and biomarker-based patient selection.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the molecular mechanisms by which human papillomaviruses (HPV) modulate the FAK-Src signalling axis, its functional consequences in HPV-associated diseases, and therapeutic opportunities. The central question is how HPV manipulates host pathways to drive cellular transformation and cancer progression.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of preclinical evidence, including studies on viral proteins such as HPV E2 and E6/E7, and their interactions with the FAK-Src axis. It outlines the methods used to investigate these interactions, such as direct protein binding, integrin signalling, and epigenetic modifications. The review does not report on clinical trials or pooled estimates but emphasizes the experimental nature of the findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that HPV proteins modulate the FAK-Src axis through various mechanisms, including inactivation of tumour suppressors, transcriptional reprogramming, and regulation of phosphatases. These interactions contribute to enhanced migration, invasion, survival, and immune modulation in HPV-associated cancers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence is limited to preclinical studies, and there is insufficient data to determine the clinical relevance of FAK-Src modulation in HPV infections. Additionally, the review notes that the role of the FAK-Src axis in different stages of the viral life cycle remains unclear.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for further research into the specific roles of the FAK-Src axis in HPV-associated diseases and the development of targeted therapies. It also suggests that understanding virus-host interactions could lead to better biomarker-based patient selection strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how human papillomaviruses (HPV) manipulate the FAK-Src signalling axis to drive cellular transformation and cancer progression. It identifies key viral proteins, such as E6/E7 and E2, that interact with this pathway through mechanisms like integrin signalling and epigenetic modifications. The review emphasizes the functional consequences of FAK-Src disruption, including enhanced migration, invasion, and immune modulation. However, it notes that the evidence is primarily preclinical, and the clinical relevance of these findings remains unclear. The review suggests that further research is needed to develop targeted therapies and biomarker-based approaches for HPV-associated diseases.

papers.abstract_zh: 肿瘤病毒通过操纵 宿主 信号通路(例如 FAK-Src 轴)在细胞转化和癌症进展中发挥作用。临床前证据表明,病毒蛋白可以通过直接相互作用、整合素信号传导、肿瘤抑制因子失活、转录和激酶重编程、钙/ROS信号传导、磷酸酶调节和表观遗传修饰来调节该轴。重要的例子包括 HPV E2 和 E6/E7、EBV LMP1 和 LMP2A、HBV HBx、HCV Core 和 E2 以及 KSHV 蛋白。FAK-Src 破坏可以激活 PI3K/AKT、Rho GTPase、AP-1 和 NF-κB 等途径,从而增强 免疫应答 的迁移、侵袭、存活、血管生成和调节。在某些感染中,该轴也可能参与病毒生命周期的不同阶段。本综述探讨了肿瘤病毒调节 FAK-Src 的分子机制及其功能和治疗意义。它还回顾了 FAK/Src 靶向策略,区分实验抑制剂、多靶点药物和临床评估下的化合物,强调每种病毒特有的有限临床证据。最后,回顾了 pFAK 和 pSrc 作为途径激活和与靶标药效相互作用的潜在标志物;然而,目前的证据不足以将其用作有效的诊断或预测生物标志物。更好地了解病毒-宿主-FAK/Src 相互作用有助于开发基于机制的治疗方法和基于生物标志物的患者选择。
papers.summary_zh: 肿瘤病毒通过操纵 宿主 信号通路(例如 FAK-Src 轴)在细胞转化和癌症进展中发挥作用。临床前证据表明,病毒蛋白可以通过直接相互作用、整合素信号传导、肿瘤抑制因子失活、转录和激酶重编程、钙/ROS信号传导、磷酸酶调节和表观遗传修饰来调节该轴。重要的例子包括 HPV E2 和 E6/E7、EBV LMP1 和 LMP2A、HBV HBx、HCV Core 和 E2 以及 KSHV 蛋白。FAK-Src 破坏可以激活 PI3K/AKT、Rho GTPase、AP-1 和 NF-κB 等途径,从而增强 免疫应答 的迁移、侵袭、存活、血管生成和调节。在某些感染中,该轴也可能参与病毒生命周期的不同阶段。本综述探讨了肿瘤病毒调节 FAK-Src 的分子机制及其功能和治疗意义。它还回顾了 FAK/Src 靶向策略,区分实验抑制剂、多靶点药物和临床评估下的化合物,强调每种病毒特有的有限临床证据。最后,回顾了 pFAK 和 pSrc 作为途径激活和与靶标药效相互作用的潜在标志物;然而,目前的证据不足以将其用作有效的诊断或预测生物标志物。更好地了解病毒-宿主-FAK/Src 相互作用有助于开发基于机制的治疗方法和基于生物标志物的患者选择。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 调节 FAK-Src 信号轴的分子机制、其在 HPV 相关疾病中的功能后果以及治疗机会。核心问题是 HPV 如何操纵 宿主 通路来驱动细胞转化和癌症进展。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对临床前证据的系统分析,包括对 HPV E2 和 E6/E7 等病毒蛋白及其与 FAK-Src 轴相互作用的研究。它概述了用于研究这些相互作用的方法,例如直接蛋白质结合、整合素信号传导和表观遗传修饰。该综述不报告临床试验或汇总估计,但强调研究结果的实验​​性质。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,HPV 蛋白通过多种机制调节 FAK-Src 轴,包括肿瘤抑制因子失活、转录重编程和磷酸酶调节。这些相互作用有助于增强 HPV 相关癌症的迁移、侵袭、存活和免疫调节。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 证据仅限于临床前研究,并且没有足够的数据来确定 FAK-Src 调节在 HPV 感染中的临床相关性。此外,该评论指出,FAK-Src 轴在病毒生命周期不同阶段的作用仍不清楚。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进一步研究 FAK-Src 轴在 HPV 相关疾病中的具体作用以及开发靶向治疗。它还表明,了解病毒-宿主 相互作用可能会导致更好的基于生物标志物的患者选择策略。

The analysis, reported in Virology Journal, also examined persistent infections, associations between particular HPV genotypes and cervical lesions, relationships with vaginal microecological disorders, and the prevalence of genotypes covered by the nine-valent HPV vaccine. The hospital-based study included female outpatients who underwent HPV genotyping from 2016 through 2021. HPV prevalence followed a bimodal age distribution, reaching its highest level among participants aged 26–30 years and showing a secondary peak among those aged 61 years or older. HPV16 was the most prevalent high-risk genotype, followed by HPV52, HPV58, HPV53 and HPV51. Because the study recruited patients at one tertiary hospital, the findings characterize the women included in the clinical sample rather than establishing population-representative HPV prevalence across Northwest China. Discover more Track Outbreaks Track Fertility Study Anatomy Persistent infection was assessed in 3,542 patients who returned for follow-up. Of these, 33.75% had persistent HPV infection, with the highest persistence rate recorded among people with mixed high-risk and low-risk HPV infections. HPV positivity was correlated with elevated abnormal rates on thin-prep cytology tests, and nine high-risk HPV genotypes were significantly associated with cytological abnormalities. In the cervical cancer cases included in the analysis, HPV16 accounted for 69.7%. These findings describe statistical associations in the retrospective cohort; they do not establish that a particular HPV genotype caused an individual cervical lesion or cancer. Check Symptoms Discover more Book a Checkup Find Vaccines vaccine Donate to Research The study also evaluated associations between HPV infection and bacterial vaginosis, aerobic vaginitis, trichomonal vaginitis, vulvovaginal candidiasis and mixed vaginitis. HPV positivity was positively associated with bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis and mixed vaginitis but inversely associated with vulvovaginal candidiasis. The strength and direction of these relationships varied by HPV subtype, indicating that the results differed among viral types. The supplied findings document associations within the analyzed patients and do not show that HPV caused a vaginal disorder or that any vaginal disorder increased HPV risk. Similarly, the reported increase in the proportion of nine-valent-vaccine-covered genotypes with increasing cervical lesion severity describes the distribution of viral genotypes in the cohort, not vaccination uptake or the vaccine’s protective effect. supplementary_news.content_title: Creative Diagnostics Introduces High-Risk HPV L1 Virus-Like Particles Produced in Yeast for Research and Assay
supplementary_news.content: Creative Diagnostics Introduces High-Risk HPV L1 Virus-Like Particles Produced in Yeast for Research and Assay Development Creative Diagnostics launches a range of High-Risk HPV L1 VLPs Produced in Yeast to support HPV research applications. New York, NY, United States - October 23, 2026 - Creative Diagnostics, a leading manufacturer and supplier of antibodies, antigens and assay kits, has launched a range of High-Risk HPV L1 VLPs Produced in Yeast [https://www.creative-diagnostics.com/high-risk-hpv-l1-vlps-produced-in-yeast.htm], a portfolio of recombinant virus-like particle (VLP) antigens to support human papillomavirus (HPV) research, serological assay development, antibody evaluation, and vaccine-related investigations. This new product line provides researchers and laboratory professionals with access to L1 VLP antigens that represent multiple high-risk HPV genotypes, which can help to advance studies of HPV-specific immune responses and antigen recognition. HPV is a non-enveloped, double-stranded DNA virus with a T=7 icosahedral capsid composed of 72 L1 pentamers (capsomeres), which are paired with L2 monomers. The L1 and L2 proteins have similar molecular weights (approximately 55kDa), with minor differences among different HPV genotypes. HPV has evolved a highly refined infection mechanism and exhibits specificity regarding the species, tissues and cell types it infects. Furthermore, the HPV virion enters the host via routes other than body fluids, resulting in a weak immune response from the host against neutralizing epitopes on the capsid. Given this low immune pressure, as well as the fact that the human antiviral immune response is primarily driven by type-specific neutralization, the HPV phylogeny is highly complex, with more than 200 distinct genotypes having accumulated to date. As there is currently no efficient method of extracting natural antigens from cultures, serological testing for HPV relies primarily on the use of "virus-like particles" (VLPs). When expressed via recombinant technology, the major HPV capsid protein L1 self-assembles into VLPs. These VLPs do not contain the viral genome, but they present type-specific conformational epitopes that are similar to those found in real viral particles. HPV L1 VLPs can induce high-titre, type-specific neutralizing antibodies and form the basis of current preventive vaccines. To better support scientific research in HPV immunology and diagnostics, Creative Diagnostics now provides researchers with high-risk HPV L1 VLPs produced in yeast, which are ideal for HPV-related research, diagnostic reagent development, antibody evaluation and viral antigen characterization. These antigens are based on the major capsid protein L1 of clinically significant high-risk HPV types. When properly expressed and processed, the L1 protein self-assembles into VLPs that resemble natural HPV capsids in structure but do not contain viral genomic material. This makes L1 VLPs non-infectious antigenic reagents that are particularly suitable for research that require the presentation of a natural capsid structure. Creative Diagnostics' new product portfolio covers nine high-risk genotypes relevant to cervical cancer research, HPV epidemiology, and immune response profiling, including HPV16, HPV18, HPV31, HPV33, HPV35, HPV45, HPV52, HPV59 and HPV68. This comprehensive testing panel enables the parallel comparison of subtype-specific antibody responses, cross-reactivity and antigenic performance across multiple high-risk genotypes. For researchers and assay developers who are interested in evaluating the High-Risk HPV L1 VLPs portfolio, product specifications, availability, application-specific requirements , or requesting bulk production, please visit https://www.creative-diagnostics.com/high-risk-hpv-l1-vlps-produced-in-yeast.htm. About Creative Diagnostics Creative Diagnostics is a leading manufacturer and supplier of antibodies, viral antigens, innovative diagnostic components, and critical assay reagents. In addition to providing contract R&D and biologic manufacturing services for diagnostic manufacturers along with GMP biologics manufacturing for the biopharmaceutical market, the company aims to continue to act as a trusted source for all researchers' assay development and manufacturing needs.
